newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Cocoa - Brazil tax relief plan welcomed by farmers.
newsitem.headline: Cocoa - Brazil tax relief plan welcomed by farmers.

text.p: Brazilian government plans to drop a sales tax on cocoa for export are good news for local farmers but could force local chocolate manufacturers to pay more for beans, traders said.

A bill introduced by planning minister Antonio Kandir to drop the 13 percent ICMS tax is currently being voted on by the Brazilian Congress and traders said that, with local elections coming up in October, they expected it to be passed.
The tax would remain in force for cocoa which stays in Brazil, which represents around 65 percent of production.
Under the present system, the buyers pay the ICMS tax but then subtract the amount from the price paid to the farmers, meaning that in practice it is the farmers who pay.
Traders said that if the tax on exports was dropped, the current price on cocoa destined for export would rise to 17 Real per 15-kg arroba from 15.5 Real.

However, traders said that Brazilian chocolate manufacturers, who would continue to pay the tax, would also have to pay the higher price for cocoa beans to enable them to compete with exporters. Farmers would therefore receive a better price for all cocoa, regardless of where it went.
